scientific_hypothesis: A depth-graded stack where bilayer thickness increases from air toward substrate will broaden the UV reflection band beyond what a periodic stack achieves, while maintaining SWIR transmission by keeping longer-period layers deeper in the stack.
expected_advantages: Broader reflection bandwidth than periodic stack
L24 shows depth-graded coatings achieve high reflectivity across wide spectral ranges
Better tolerance to wavelength shift from angle variation
known_risks: Graded stacks require more precise thickness control during deposition
May introduce more absorption if HfO2 layers become too thick
L26 notes defect formation in HfO2 films can affect optical properties
expected_observations: If the chirped hypothesis holds, best_target_score should show higher final values than route_01 and tightest_margin should remain stable or improve across rounds
If the chirped hypothesis fails, best_target_score will not exceed route_01's performance and thickness gradient parameters will converge to near-zero (effectively becoming periodic)
valid_candidates should remain above 8 per round if the gradient parameterization is well-posed
thicknesses_nm should show monotonic increase from air to substrate if the chirped structure is optimal
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
If the optimized thickness gradient converges to less than 1 nm per bilayer, the chirped advantage is not realized; stop and flag this axis as not beneficial over periodic
